title: Length of a Billing Cycle When a Rider is Closed
content:
How many coverage months a billing cycle carries on one of the Optional Supplemental Benefit Riders, when the rider is closed, follows from the member's Medicare Advantage Health Plans enrollment — whether it stands in force and how often it is billed.

## The rule

**Where the medical plan enrollment the rider hangs on stands in force and is billed quarterly**, a billing cycle carries three coverage months.

**Where that enrollment does not stand in force**, a billing cycle carries the whole calendar months from the day the rider took effect to the handling date, and never fewer than one.

**Otherwise**, a billing cycle carries a single coverage month.

## Condition and coverage months

| What the Medicare Advantage Health Plans enrollment shows | Coverage months a billing cycle carries |
|---|---|
| In force, billed quarterly | 3 |
| In force, billed other than quarterly | 1 |
| Not in force | The whole calendar months from the day the rider took effect to the handling date, never fewer than 1 |

## Worked on hypothetical inputs

- An enrollment standing in force and billed quarterly: 3 coverage months.
- An enrollment standing in force and billed monthly: 1 coverage month.
- An enrollment no longer standing in force, the rider having taken effect 8 whole calendar months before the handling date: 8 coverage months.
- An enrollment no longer standing in force, the rider having taken effect in the month of handling: 1 coverage month, that being the floor.

Unlike the other two cases, the second case here turns on the enrollment's standing alone and takes no account of what the rider premium account carries.
